title: a tool declares the risk it carries, and the rule asks by the declaration
intent: The wave B1 of the track B: the specification of a tool carries the field `:risk', and the list of the tools that change the world moves out of a hand-written list of names and into the declarations of the tools themselves.  The kernel is touched: one new module (`lib/yeah-risk.el', 113 lines, 4 799 bytes) owns the vocabulary of the risk and the question `does this tool change the world?', twelve modules of the kernel declare the risk of their tools (25 declarations in 10 modules), and the profile of the permission rule asks by those declarations and not by a list of names.  The vocabulary is four words -- `read', `write', `execute' and `destroy'.  A tool that declares no risk has a risk that is not known, and a risk that is not known changes the world: the rule asks about it, and the absence of a declaration never makes the rule softer.  A tool that declares a risk outside the vocabulary is refused by name at the registration.  **The late binding breaks the circle of the requires**: the registry of the tools requires the modules that require the permission rule, and the permission rule asks by the declarations that live in the registry, so the module of the risk knows only the vocabulary and the question, and the registry installs the source of the declarations into it (`yeah-risk--install-source').  **The check measures the set and does not take it from a constant**: `tests/checks/check-a-tool-declares-its-own-risk.el' (1129 lines, 49 546 bytes) follows the calls of the handler of every tool of the core -- a small interpreter over the forms of Elisp that binds the parameters and the local variables, remembers the process that the tool started itself, and tells the text that the model supplied from the text that the kernel supplied -- and looks for the primitives that change the world.  The check proves six things: (1) every tool of the core declares a risk of the vocabulary; (2) the registration refuses a risk outside the vocabulary and accepts a tool that declares no risk; (3) the declaration of a tool agrees with what its handler does -- the set of the tools that the measurement finds changing the world is the set of the tools that declare a risk other than `read'; (4) the category the declaration names is one of the categories the measurement found; (5) the rule asks by the declaration -- the profiles name exactly the tools the measurement found, a probe that declares `read' is not named, a probe that declares `write' is named and a probe that declares nothing is named; (6) an action that no rule names is asked about and is never allowed.  The sixth is the parent's strengthening: the profile is a snapshot and the safety of a snapshot rests on the default of the rule, and nothing held that default before.
objection: The claim is about the declaration and about the rule that asks by it, and not about the safety of the agent in general.  The price is named and it is six prices.  (a) **The measurement is an over-approximation**: the check names every category that the handler of a tool may reach and never names a category that it does not reach; a read tool that the measurement finds changing the world is a defect of the declaration, and a mutating tool whose declaration is one of the categories that the measurement found is a declaration that agrees with the handler.  (b) **The locality of a process is a heuristic at the level of the tool**: a tool that started a process and also stopped a foreign one is measured without `destroy', and the check says so in its commentary.  (c) **The result layer is not walked**: `lib/yeah-result.el' writes the artifact of a long output for every tool of the kernel, so walking it would make every tool look like it changes the world.  (d) **The profile is a snapshot and the approval path keeps a list of its own**: `lib/yeah-approval.el:74-94' still holds a hand-written list of the safe reads (`yeah-approval-safe-read-actions', 9 names), so the tools that declare `read' and are not in that list (`todo_list', `delegate-result', `git_status', `git_diff') are still asked about in the attached path; that is the same class of drift as the list this wave removes, it is the next step of B1, and the claim of this wave does not speak about it -- the scope of the claim is the profile of the permission rule and not the path of the approval.  (e) **The behaviour of the Plan profile grew and the growth is named**: the profile now forbids two tools more, `todo_add' and `todo_update', that the hand-written list never named and that the rule therefore asked about; the decision of the parent is dated 2026-11-21 and the owner may cancel it (docs/PLAN.md section 16.90).  (f) **The claim is new and not amended**: the claim `a-tool-declares-its-own-risk' is new in this wave, and the strengthening of the parent is in the check and in the text of the claim, not in a second promise.
refuted_by: the rule asks by a list of names and not by the declaration, or the declaration of a tool and the handler of that tool disagree: a tool of the core that declares no risk, a tool that declares a risk outside the vocabulary of the kernel and is accepted, a tool that changes the world and declares the risk `read', a tool that changes nothing and declares a risk other than `read', a tool that declares a category the measurement of its handler did not find, a profile that names a tool the measurement did not find or that misses a tool the measurement found, a probe that declares the risk `read' and is asked about anyway, a probe that declares that it changes the world and is not asked about, or an action that no rule names that is allowed instead of asked about, or the control of the claim does not make the check fail by its own assertion
note: The wave gave the tools a declaration and took the list of names away from the rule.  (1) **The module of the risk**: `lib/yeah-risk.el', 113 lines, 4 799 bytes -- the vocabulary `("read" "write" "execute" "destroy")' as a constant, `yeah-risk-known-p', `yeah-risk-of', `yeah-risk-mutating-p', `yeah-risk-mutating-tools' and the late binding `yeah-risk--install-source'.  The module requires only `cl-lib' and loads the registry on demand, so the circle of the requires does not close; the registry installs the source of the declarations at the end of its own load, and `yeah-perm--mutating-tools' signals `user-error' when the declarations are not known, because a rule that allows what it does not know is not a rule.  (2) **The declarations**: 25 of them in 10 modules -- `lib/yeah-files.el' (3), `lib/yeah-edit.el' (2), `lib/yeah-process.el' (4), `lib/yeah-emacs.el' (4), `lib/yeah-todo.el' (3), `lib/yeah-git.el' (3), `lib/yeah-trash.el' (1), `lib/yeah-builtins.el' (1), `lib/yeah-delegate.el' (2) and `lib/yeah-bridge.el' (2); the registry refuses a risk outside the vocabulary by name and accepts a tool that declares none.  (3) **The rule**: `yeah-perm--mutating-tools' became a function, and the profiles `plan' and `build' ask by the declarations -- the set the profiles name is the set the measurement finds, and the probe of the check proves that the rule follows the declaration and not the name.  (4) **The check**: `tests/checks/check-a-tool-declares-its-own-risk.el', 1129 lines, 49 546 bytes, 6 proofs; the exit codes are 0 (the declarations agree with the handlers and with the rule) and 1 (they do not).  (5) **The controls of the parent, five on copies of the tree, 2026-11-21**: a risk outside the vocabulary (`lib/yeah-files.el', `:risk "source"') -- the code 1 and the refusal `not in the vocabulary of the kernel'; the declaration taken away -- the code 1 and the refusal `the tool "read" declares no risk'; a tool that changes nothing that declares `write' -- the code 1 and the refusal `its handler changes nothing: it reaches nothing'; a tool that changes the world that declares `read' -- the code 1 and the refusal `the tool "edit" changes the world -- its handler reaches ("write") -- but it declares the risk "read"'; the honest tree -- the code 0.  (6) **The control of another claim died and was transferred**: the control of `the-plan-profile-denies-a-delegation' mutated the list of names that this wave removes, so it changed nothing and the check passed -- the class of F38, a guard that never fires; it now mutates the declaration of the risk of the delegation (`sed -i 's|:risk "write"|:risk "read"|' lib/yeah-delegate.el'), and the parent measured that the unit test of the delegation fails with the code 1; the text, the falsifier, the scope, the requirements and the id of that claim are the same.  (7) **The picture of the wave 97 had to be re-anchored, and the strengthened check said so**: the wave moved the lines of `lib/', three names of `site/diagrams/core-layers.puml' left their definitions (`lib/yeah-perm.el:62' to `:68', `lib/yeah-tools.el:118' to `:119', `lib/yeah-delegate.el:428' to `:430') and the new module `lib/yeah-risk.el' was not named; the check of the wave 97 named all four, because the parent strengthened it on 2026-11-21 to hold that a reference names a definition and not merely a line with code; the parent compared all 64 names with a snapshot of the state before the wave -- 59 did not move, 2 moved on the same definition (the signature changed) and 3 left -- and the picture now carries 65 names.  (8) **The remainder of B1 is named and not hidden**: the list of the safe reads of the approval path (`lib/yeah-approval.el:74-94') is still a list of names, and the next step of B1 is to make it follow the declarations as well.
